newsitem.title: UK: Southern Air to acquire more B747 freighters.
newsitem.headline: Southern Air to acquire more B747 freighters.

text.p: Privately-owned U.S. all-cargo carrier Southern Air Transport says it will introduce into service a fourth Boeing 747-200 freighter in August and up to five more by 2000.

The fourth aircraft, a passenger 747, is being leased on a long-term contract from an unnamed U.S. company and will undergo conversion work into full-freighter configuration in May for introduction into service in August, said senior vice-president Asa Hemperley.
The conversion contract would "probably" go to Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering Company (HAECO), he added.
The majority of the new acquisitions will probably also be existing passenger aircraft needing conversion into freighters.

"We are scanning the globe for suitable aircraft. We want our whole commercial fleet to be based on 747-200 freighters in the future, if we can find them," he said noting competition is tough whenever a 747-200F freighter comes up for sale.

Southern wet-leases out its present commercial cargo fleet of 747Fs and four DC-8 freighters to customers including South African Airways SAA.CN, Japan Airlines and Frontier de Colombia, parent of Colombian flower exporting company Aerofloral.
Wet-leasing covers the hire of both aircraft and crew.
The carrier also operates 15 Lockheed L10-100 Hercules freighters, mainly for relief and other emergency work.
"For the new aircraft we are talking to a number of potential customers," said Hemperley.
"These include Singapore Airlines and Qantas . We have flown DC-8 freighters in the past on their behalf and hope they might upgrade to our 747F service," he told Reuters.
"We are also looking to JAL and Frontier for extra (747F wet-leasing) business," he added.
-Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
